summary: Picus Breach and Attack Simulation (formerly Security Control Validation): it safely and continuously attacks your own controls and shows what they miss.
value: It shows which attacks the firewall, WAF, EDR and email protection really block and which get through.
For every gap there are ready-made signatures and rules for 12 vendors.
After the fix the attack is replayed to prove the protection works.
simple: The core product of the Picus platform (formerly the Security Control Validation module, SCV): safely and continuously attacks your own security tools — NGFW and IPS firewalls, WAF, antivirus and EDR/XDR, email security, DLP, proxies — and shows what each of them blocks, what it detects and what slips through. The attacks are real malicious files and actions, not replayed traffic: 2,900+ malicious file downloads, 2,500+ phishing emails with attachments and links, 350+ web application attacks, scenarios on Windows (95+ ATT&CK techniques), Linux and macOS, data exfiltration over HTTP(S), DNS and SMTP, and URL filtering checks. The Picus Labs threat library (30,000+ techniques and procedures) is updated almost daily, critical threats within 24 hours; AI turns a threat report, CVE or threat-group name into a ready simulation in minutes. The attack participants are Picus agents attacking each other, not production systems. Through APIs with 23 SIEM and EDR products (Splunk, QRadar, Sentinel, CrowdStrike, Defender, SentinelOne, Cortex XDR) it checks whether the attack was logged and whether an alert was raised. For every gap it provides ready-made signatures for 12 vendors (Check Point, Cisco, Fortinet, Palo Alto, F5, Imperva, Trend Micro and others) and detection rules (including SIGMA), then repeats the same attack to prove the gap is closed. Results go on a MITRE ATT&CK map and into executive reports. It can also test the protection of AI applications: prompt injections, jailbreaks and MCP tool abuse.
classification: The BAS class was created for Picus: it does not protect by itself but tests protection; defenses[] are only techniques the modules explicitly simulate.
AI Security Validation is part of BAS and stays in the text.
